correctness.rationale: All definitions and quantifiers are explicit for integer exponent vectors with k>=2 and 2<=j,m<=k. Inclusion-exclusion independently derives c_j; selecting two prime coordinates produces a sum of products of complete symmetric polynomials with coefficients that are nonnegative combinations of Schur polynomials. The adjacent-exponent coefficient difference is exactly the Schur coefficient for shape (L-b-1,b+1), and an admissible outsider assignment plus degree profile dominated by that shape ensures strictly positive Kostka multiplicity at every j. This is an infinite proof, not a finite enumeration inference. A deterministic injective prime-support split with a second unused allocation proves the cross-support strictness. All positive Stirling coefficients are a published identity. Exact code independently checks 16422 transfers and 169910 inequalities for each of the two count families; brute exponent-matrix checks ensure the formulas are implemented correctly. Boundary cases k=r and r=1, nonunit factors, and m>k are stated.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 literature asks for computable divisor-function and sum-system counts and supplies an exact Stirling transform; a natural missing extremal question is which integer prime-exponent signatures maximize or minimize every such count at fixed Ω and fixed ω. The result gives one transfer operation that strictly improves every coefficient and every m-part sum-system count at once, with unique exact endpoint classifications, including variable support. This is stronger than total ordered-factorization monotonicity, the top-length multinomial optimization, or a routine known-table recomputation. The proof uses an actual strict Schur-coefficient witness instead of inferring positivity from an alternating formula. The precise arithmetic extremizers can be substituted in the explicit formulas for further values; the contribution is a motivated structural comparison principle, not an unsupported downstream conjecture.
